abstract:
Astronomers find about 5.4 times as much dark matter as ordinary matter. [[c:dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent]] In this framework the dark matter lives in separate towers that touch ours only through gravity. [[c:pred.dark-matter-direct-detection-null]]

This trail meets the towers, the mirror tower that copies ours, and the reason their matter stays dark and never decays. [[t]] Under its premises the mirror accounts for one unit of the dark matter, a copy of ordinary matter to within half a percent. [[c:dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent]]

A counting rule then matches the full observed ratio, but it is recorded as a fit, not a prediction. [[c:dark-matter.status-rule]] The walk ends by setting the dark sector, as the series builds it, against the data, where no arrangement yet passes every test. [[c:dark-tower-matter.towers-built]]
introduction:
The walk first sets out which dark towers exist and why they stay dark, then turns to how much matter they hold and what it is made of. [[t]]

It closes with tests against observations. [[t]]
i:dark-matter: Each step below either says what the dark towers are or checks what they should do. [[t]]
t:^>dark-matter.towers-are-residues-sing:
Real Clifford algebras repeat with period eight, and the series reads each repeating family as a tower. [[t]] Along a tower the residue \[ p - q \pmod 8 \] is invariant, with $p$ and $q$ the numbers of positive and negative directions. [[c:dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter]]

Taking each tower at the dimension nearest four (premise P3), exactly the residues $0$ and $4$ lack a single time direction, the two-time case excluded by importing the standard instability. [[c:dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter]] That leaves six towers that admit matter: ours and five dark ones. [[c:dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter]]
t:dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single:
The closest dark tower is the mirror, reached by reversing the signature, so that time and space directions swap roles. [[c:dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one]] Every input of the Standard-Model chain is invariant under that reversal, so the mirror carries its own copy of the derived Standard Model. [[c:dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one]]

With a common ceiling and under the single frozen point (P1) and indifference (P2), \[ \Omega_{\mathrm{mirror}} = \Omega_{b} \] to half a percent, where $\Omega_{b}$ is the ordinary (baryonic) matter density. [[c:dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one]] A cold mirror is, however, an exception to that same indifference, which would otherwise make the mirror as hot as ours. [[c:dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one]]
t:dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one>dark:
A copy of our world raises the question of why we cannot see it. [[t]]

Under P1, the sector decomposition and the wall-sequence theorem's hypotheses (a compact base and good couplings), the tower charge is exactly superselected, so dark-tower matter is exactly stable. [[c:dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable]] That it only gravitates, at first order, comes from the series' acoustic no-go, conditional on the Indifference premise and premise (Q). [[c:dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable]]
t:dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-e:
This gives the trail its first prediction. [[t]]

Direct-detection searches should stay null permanently, because dark matter couples to ordinary matter through gravity alone at first order. [[c:pred.dark-matter-direct-detection-null]] The expectation is conditional on the single-frozen-point premise and on the acoustic no-go. [[c:pred.dark-matter-direct-detection-null]]
t:pred.dark-matter-direct-detection-null:
The next question is how much dark matter the towers hold. [[t]] Under P1 to P4, with every tower's matter diluting as ours, the mirror supplies an asymmetric dark share of one $\Omega_{b}$ to half a percent. [[c:dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent]]

That leaves a symmetric remainder of \[ 4.364\,\Omega_{b} \] which is not derived. [[c:dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent]]
t:dark-matter.population-count-one-share:
A separate counting rule attempts the whole ratio. [[t]] Under premises R1 to R3, each populated tower holds one quantum of a common mass per unit ball of its own space, so a tower with $D$-dimensional space has share $V_{3}/V_{D}$, with $V_{D}$ the volume of the unit ball. [[c:dark-matter.unit-ball-rule]]

Summed over the towers, the dark-to-baryon ratio is \[ \frac{11\pi + 16}{3\pi} \approx 5.3643, \] against the observed $5.364 \pm 0.065$. [[c:dark-matter.unit-ball-rule]]
t:dark-matter.unit-ball-rule>dark-matter:
A close match calls for caution rather than celebration. [[t]]

The relation was found by fitting, and it is one of fourteen equally simple values within the error bar of one Planck column. [[c:dark-matter.status-rule]] It rests on premises R1 to R3 and on the costed clause that empties residues $0$ and $4$, so it is recorded as a fit at observation level, not a prediction. [[c:dark-matter.status-rule]]
t:dark-matter.status-rule>dark-tower-mat:
The counting rule says how much matter the dark towers hold, but not what that matter is made of. [[t]] Repeating our own construction, mass begins at two constituents in dimensions three and four and at one constituent in dimension five. [[c:dark-tower-matter.where-mass-begins]]

Under premise H2 and Premise U the gauge algebra is \[ \so(2) \oplus \so(2) \] in the three-dimensional towers and $\uu(3) = \su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$ in the five-dimensional towers. [[c:dark-tower-matter.gauge-algebras]] Reading a constituent's momentum from its spinor is established in our tower but a premise in three and five dimensions (premise H1). [[c:dark-tower-matter.h1-momentum]]
Abelian dark forces raise the question of dark radiation, which the early universe limits. [[t]] The three-dimensional towers' radiation channels close, while the mirror and five-dimensional channels stay open. [[c:dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem-closes-what]]

The framework predicts \[ \Delta\Neff \approx 0 \] conditionally on those open channels closing, which holds if the descent's deposit is no hotter than estimated, and on a cold mirror, an exception to P2. [[c:pred.no-dark-radiation]]
t:pred.no-dark-radiation>dark-tower-matt:
The last step puts the whole dark sector, as the series builds it, against the data. [[t]]

At observation level no configuration of the five dark towers as built passes every test. [[c:dark-tower-matter.towers-built]] The least exposed needs four choices the series does not make, and it stays $1.24$ above Roux and Cline's limit. [[c:dark-tower-matter.towers-built]]
conclusion:
Along the trail, the dark matter is the content of hidden towers felt only through gravity, with the mirror supplying one unit of it and the symmetric remainder left underived. [[c:dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent]] As built, no arrangement of the dark towers yet passes every test against the data. [[c:dark-tower-matter.towers-built]]

The trail rests on stated premises: a single frozen point (P1), indifference (P2), nearest-dimension representatives (P3), an evenly shared asymmetry (P4), Hypothesis (S) behind the mirror's copy, the counting premises R1 to R3, premises H1, H2 and U behind the odd towers' forces, and Hypothesis (U) behind the radiation audit. [[t]] The predictions of null searches and no extra radiation are conditional on those premises, and a confirmed signal would count against them. [[t]]
